Planning help

Get your sizes right the first time

What to measure for the most common projects, and how to get a second set of eyes on it.

Hero image
Overhead shot of a hand-drawn room sketch with dimensions, a tape measure and a material sample on a kitchen table, natural light.

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, once you've picked a material, size is the next big decision. Here's what to have on paper before you order. Treat it as a starting point; each product page lists the exact specs.

What to measure

Ceiling beams

Room length and width, ceiling height, which way the joists run, and how many beams you're picturing.

Shutters

Height and width of every window opening. Measure each one, even if they look identical.

Mantels and corbels

Width and height of the wall or fireplace, and what the piece will hold. Check the specs before anything rests on it.

Moulding and trim

Length of each wall, ceiling height, and a count of inside and outside corners.

Columns

Floor-to-ceiling height, and whether it's decorative or needs to carry weight. The specs will tell you.
